acceptance_criteria: WORKSPACE MODE DONE 2026-11-06: 'storypole config check --workspace' audits every suite member in one pass, which is what the eleven-empty-configs sweep was done by hand to find. Membership from WorkspaceTopology, never a glob. A repository with no configuration is skipped rather than reported, since not being adopted yet is not a defect; the run fails only if no repository carries a config at all, which means it was pointed at the wrong tree. Reads through load_unified_or_legacy so an audit leaves no index files behind. Observed: 10 repositories audited, 0 findings, 0 errors - common correctly excluded.\n\nWhat this now makes mechanical: the exact question 'does every repo's config claim what it delivers' that required reading eleven files by hand earlier in this session.

task.title: Add a config validator: empty or inconsistent fields should be reported, not silently accepted

acceptance_criteria: from a manual sweep across eleven configs: verification_commands was empty in all eleven (so verify silently ran 'cargo test')
allowed_repos was [] in ten and ["storypole"] in one (semantically 'unrestricted' vs 'scoped'
with nothing saying which was intended)
and allowed_crates was [] everywhere and appears unenforced. ticket_prefix was correct in all eleven. Findings that a validator could report

and that cost several manual passes to establish: empty verification_commands; a prefix that collides with another repo in the same suite; allowed_repos naming a repo that does not exist; a field that is present but unenforced. Shape: 'storypole config check [--workspace]' with warnings
except for genuine breakage - the point is that 'present but empty' stops being invisible.

RULES LANDED 2026-11-06 (storypole-core commit): StorypoleConfig::audit returns ConfigFinding { field, message, severity }. Warnings for weakened-but-working config (empty verification_commands, duplicate entries, claim_ttl_minutes 0, a path in allowed_repos, a non-upper-case prefix); errors only where the config cannot behave as written (empty prefix, an empty command that would let verify pass by doing nothing). Six tests including a healthy config that reports nothing - an audit that always finds something is one nobody reads. Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 6/6.

Deliberately not reported: unset allowed_repos. Empty means unrestricted (config.rs:101 skips the check), which is legitimate for a meta-harness root; warning there would dilute the signal.

REMAINING: the 'storypole config check [--json]' subcommand is a thin adapter and is not wired yet. It can reuse print_json now that GB-274 landed, so the output shape is already decided.

DONE 2026-11-06 (storypole commit). 'storypole config check [--json]' wired as a subcommand of the new 'storypole config' group, delegating to StorypoleConfig::audit. JSON output goes through the GB-274 envelope ({command, errors, findings, schema_version}).

Exit discipline: zero for warnings, non-zero only for errors. A warning means the configuration works but claims more than it delivers; failing a build over that would train people to pass a flag instead of reading the output, which is how gates die.

Verified twice: on this repository ('Configuration looks sound: no findings.', exit 0) and on a temp repo with empty verification_commands, which produced the exact warning the eleven-config sweep had to be done by hand to find - 'verification_commands is empty, so storypole verify falls back to cargo test' - exit 0. Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 55/55.

FOLLOW-UP not done: a --workspace mode that audits every repository in one pass, which is what would catch the eleven-config case mechanically. Single-repo is the 90% case and the fleet read can reuse GB-263's topology plumbing.

WORKSPACE MODE DONE 2026-11-06: 'storypole config check --workspace' audits every suite member in one pass, which is what the eleven-empty-configs sweep was done by hand to find. Membership from WorkspaceTopology, never a glob. A repository with no configuration is skipped rather than reported, since not being adopted yet is not a defect; the run fails only if no repository carries a config at all, which means it was pointed at the wrong tree. Reads through load_unified_or_legacy so an audit leaves no index files behind. Observed: 10 repositories audited, 0 findings, 0 errors - common correctly excluded.\n\nWhat this now makes mechanical: the exact question 'does every repo's config claim what it delivers' that required reading eleven files by hand earlier in this session.
